name: Texas Legislature — SB 1188 (89R), Health & Safety Code §183.005: Artificial intelligence in electronic health records (diagnostic use)
quote: A health care practitioner may use artificial intelligence for diagnostic purposes, including the use of artificial intelligence for recommendations on a diagnosis or course of treatment based on a patient's medical record, if:
quote_label: Tex. Health & Safety Code §183.005(a), added by SB 1188 (89R), enrolled text (Act effective September 1, 2025); read live 2026-11-22

provenance.note: DISCONFIRMATION PROBE (machine-permitted-where-proof-is-scarce). Probe result: partly holds. Diagnosis is scarce-proof work, and the statute expressly permits AI for it. The conditions are (1) acting within the practitioner's license 'regardless of the use of artificial intelligence', (2) the use is not otherwise prohibited, and (3) the practitioner 'reviews all records created with artificial intelligence' to Texas Medical Board records standards. The guard is license-bound accountability (relational) plus review of the record (cheap proof). It demands no evidence that the diagnostic recommendation is accurate (D6=0). D1=0: no AI provenance or logging duty. D2=2: license scope 'regardless of the use of artificial intelligence'. D3=2: 'must disclose the practitioner's use of that technology to the practitioner's patients'. D4=0. D5=2: review of all AI-created records. D6=0. Enabling posture.
